reason: Every session ends at once: each refresh family is revoked, every push token is forgotten, and tokens_invalid_before moves to the next whole second, so an access token already issued is 401 on its next request. A sign-in whose password check straddles the act is re-checked under the sessions lock and is undone or refused (ruling 7); a sign-in or a refresh mints its access token under that lock, so the act stamps after it and the token dies with the rest. One request already authenticated completes. Nobody tells the member: no email, no push, and every way back in answers what a wrong password answers.
evidenceRef: SuspendedMemberTest#a suspended member is locked out, and the sign-in refusal is a wrong password's
